refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: The systemd-tpm2-swtpm.service provides fallback software TPM functionality, intended for use in environments where a discrete or firmware TPM ("hardware TPM") is not available. It is pulled into the boot process by systemd-tpm2-generator8 if a hardware TPM is not available, and the system is configured to provide a software TPM in that case.

Note that a software TPM provides only very weak security properties compared to a hardware TPM, and hence should only be used as a fallback mechanism if a hardware TPM is not available but TPM semantics are desired. This service ultimately wraps swtpm8.

If the boot secret /.extra/boot-secret (in the initrd) or /run/systemd/stub/boot-secret (on the host) is available the software TPM NVRAM storage is encrypted with this key. See systemd-stub7 for details.
The TPM NVRAM storage is placed on the EFI System Partition as it needs to be accessible during very early boot-up, in particular before the root file system is decrypted and mounted.

The service allocates the kernel vTPM proxy device (i.e. /dev/tpm0 and /dev/tpmrm0) itself, passes it to swtpm, and keeps it in the service's file descriptor store (see FileDescriptorStoreMax= and FileDescriptorStorePreserve= in systemd.service5). This way the TPM device continues to exist while the service is stopped, in particular across the transition from the initrd to the host, and across service restarts, and keeps its device number. TPM commands issued while the service is not running are processed once it is started again. Note that this is also the case for a command that timed out in the meantime: even though an error has been reported to the issuing client already, it is still executed by the software TPM once the service is started again. If the service fails permanently, the device is released. Since the software TPM is only intended as fallback for systems without a TPM, the service fails if the allocated device is not /dev/tpm0, i.e. if some other TPM device already exists.
